properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 6:19AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
have caused portions of that snowfall to melt creating many slushy
areas of melting snow and pooling water. Overnight low
temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning are expected to
fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will allow much of this
slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very likely Wednesday
morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles freeze. Areas of
heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the slush a sturdier,
more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted, especially during
the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.

heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 27 at 2:54AM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:

today through at least Wednesday night. Heavy rain and isolated
thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding, and while the
greatest flood threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all
islands are at risk.

possible.

* WHEN...From 6 AM HST this morning through late Wednesday night.

streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
are expected to develop today and continue through Wednesday
night as a trough moves over the state. While the greatest flood
threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are
at risk.

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
